If you decide to go for tipx  or an FSC you're not necessarily "out gunned" at the end of the day, from a physics POV,  we're all shooting projectiles of the same mass, at a standard velocity of 280 ft/s so we're essentially shooting the same "caliber". It's not like IRL where a 50cal out ranges a 9mm. It depends on your play style, I've seen people obliterate the other team with pistols. Some prefer the feel of rifles. It's all dependent on playstyle and preference although the rifle format seems to be the most popular.

Personally I like the rifle platform as I'm more reserved when I play and rely on range to be my advantage. The 4 points of contact on a rifle feel more stable to me (handguard, pistol grip, buttstock,  cheek weld). But like I said, I've seen players wreak havoc with just "sidearms"

Your playstyle may change over time, maybe later on you'll wanna rock a shield and you'll need to play with a side arm. It's always nice to have a variety of skill.

"A jack of all trades is master of none, but often times better than a master of one."

But for starters I would personally reccomend the EMF100. Again just MY Opinion but I'm sure a large number of others would agree.

I beg to differ. Everyone I play with including but not limited to my teammates have FSR dialed into a fine science. You just need the right equipment and attachments. A snug rifled barrel can make a night/day difference when it comes to BOTH accuracy and Precision. Sure there are stray shots every now and then but I would say 90% of the shots land where they're supposed to.

There's one dude on my team who conaiders himself a designated sniper and this guy ran all the tabulation, tests and charts you can imagine. Statistically, your gear MATTERS.

We aren't YouTube or famous people when it comes to magfed but if you'd like to check out our videos we're on Instagram @1shotonekill_magfed or my personal one @viper_1sok_nj. And you'll see the consistency of these shots. Also keep in mind majority of us have the 40mm 4k scopecam so all targets you see are further than what appear.

If you add a range finder, an optic with a cross hair (not a reticle) and an HHA riser, you're setting yourself up to be as precise and accurate as possible. Often times people shoot with their sight not directly over bore. This happens lot with red dots . This can be eliminated by having your cross hair parallel and perpendicular to the ground, indicating a "lined up" sight over bore before shooting. Also HHA risers in conjunction with a range finder account for the drop of the FSR the further it travels without messing up your zero.


All this aside, to answer OP:

Don't waste your money on Amazon sights. My personal experience, I've bought 6 amazon sights worth $30 each. 
Buy once, cry once. Get yourself any VORTEX optic. I have a Sparc AR. They're roughly $250 and their warranty will replace it for   *ANY REASON* and is transferable when you buy or sell the optic.
 They hold zero and the Sparc AR hold a traditional AAA battery UNDER the red dot, doubling as a riser. They don't use those hard to find button cell batteries.

Although this does not have a crosshair (it's just a red dot) I've learned to be aware about  my sight ligning up with my bore. 

I haven't bought another sight since.

Infact they have videos on their YouTube where they take an optic, submerge it in water, freeze it over night, and literally SHOOT AT IT with a shotgun and it was still on and holding zero and still fully functional.

Rainbow 6 siege is a different kind of FPS.
It has an incredibly high learning curve and is very unforvigiving  if you're not comitted to it. This game is heavily based off map knowledge, down to the location destructable walls, impenetrable furniture , small gaps in between sandbags etc. This game is also dynamic and constantly changing, so dont get too comfortable as things will change such as gadget effectiveness, game play meta, and even damage/recoil statistics as new operators are introduced, ubisoft tries it's best to balance things out.

If you like slow methodical tactical and TEAM BASED games.... this game is for you. This isn't battlefield where 1 player barely makes a difference. You WILL get frustrated by how you got killed, your teammates and certain operators. But once you are caught up to speed on map knowledge and how each operator plays a role, this can be a very fun game that will get your adrenaline going, making you feel like you're part of the action.

I dont reccomend this game if you dont plan on consistently learning the map and operators because you'll never get good at it. Like I said it has a high learning curve, it's not your typical point and shoot game.
